entities.summary:
Remigius of Rouen was the illegitimate son of Charles Martel and an unknown mistress.

As the third archbishop of Rouen from 755 to 772, Remigius played a crucial role in shaping the religious landscape of Francia during the Carolingian Renaissance.

His tenure was marked by significant architectural projects, including the restoration of the Abbey of Saint-Victor and the construction of a new cathedral in Rouen.

Remigius' legacy extends beyond his own diocese, as he helped to promote the ideals of the Carolingian Renaissance throughout Francia, influencing the development of monasticism and the spread of Christianity.

The passing of Remigius in 771 CE marked the beginning of a new era for the Archdiocese of Rouen, one that would be shaped by the subsequent leadership of his successors.

As an illegitimate son of Charles Martel, Remigius' life was marked by the intrigue and power struggles of the Carolingian court, yet he remained committed to his faith and his role as a spiritual leader.

The exact date of Remigius' birth remains unknown, but his impact on the history of Francia is undeniable.
